title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Kiribati: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Kiribati: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Kiribati: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: Planning legal, healthcare, workplace, and financial administration in advance in Kiribati helps families prepare orderly records before urgent medical transitions occur. Because the Ministry of Health and Medical Services (MHMS) and Kiribati Judiciary websites publish institutional directories rather than online advance-directive or step-by-step probate portals, this guide relies on primary Kiribati statutes, Kiribati Provident Fund (KPF) withdrawal rules, Public Service Office conditions, and accredited regional consular documentation [1][2][5][8][10].

steps.title: Healthcare coordination, palliative capacity, and statutory workplace leave
steps.html:
• Coordinate clinical care, hospital referrals, and medical assessments through Ministry of Health and Medical Services (MHMS) at Nawerewere (Tungaru Central Hospital, South Tarawa), noting emergency numbers of 994 for medical ambulance, 992 for police, and 993 for fire [1][10][12]. Confirm specialist and palliative support options early, as specialized hospital mortuary storage, embalming, and domestic medical subspecialties on Tarawa and the outer islands are limited [10].
  • Review statutory leave entitlements under the Employment and Industrial Relations Code 2015 (EIRC 2015), which grants employees with at least 6 months of continuous service up to 20 working days of paid sick leave per year under Section 93 (supported by a medical certificate from a qualified practitioner) and 3 working days of paid compassionate leave per year under Section 94 to care for a seriously ill immediate family member or following a family loss [5][6].
  • Public-sector employees should also verify agency leave, extended medical-board, and accrued leave payout provisions under the National Conditions of Service (NCS) overseen by the Public Service Office [7].

steps.title: Drafting a Will, land-tenure rules, and legal proxy limits
steps.html:
• Prepare or review a clear written Will covering cash, bank deposits, vehicles, and personal property, and confirm with a Kiribati legal practitioner whether separate Island Council or Lands Court steps apply to customary land [8]. Under the Native Lands Ordinance (Cap. 61), native land interests follow statutory transfer restrictions and Lands Court jurisdiction rather than unrestricted testamentary transfer [8].
  • Clarify the limits of medical decision-making proxies in advance: Kiribati lacks a widely digitalized statutory health-care proxy registry, so families should discuss treatment preferences directly with the attending MHMS physician while the patient retains legal capacity [1][10].
  • Identify where original property deeds, leases, and signed estate papers are held, and record contact details for the High Court registry under Kiribati Judiciary so executors or next of kin know where formal applications are filed [10][11][14].

steps.title: Kiribati Provident Fund (KPF) nominations and incapacity or death benefits
steps.html:
• Check and update beneficiary records directly with Kiribati Provident Fund (KPF) (+686 74021153) using an official KPF Nomination Form supported by birth or marriage certificates for each nominee [4]. Keeping a valid nomination avoids delays, because if a nominee is under 18 KPF transfers the entitlement to the Kiribati Lands Board, and if no valid nomination exists KPF remits the balance to the Kiribati High Court [4].
  • Where serious illness permanently prevents continued employment, review KPF Full Withdrawal on Medical Incapacity grounds: applicants submit the KPF Illness Full Withdrawal Form, a KPF Medical Examination Form completed by an MHMS doctor, a general enquiry interview sheet, and a valid KPF ID card for direct bank payment, offset against any active KPF loan or pledge [2].
  • Note also KPF's Special Death Benefit partial withdrawal rule ($1,500.00, or 50% of the unpledged balance if insufficient funds exist), which reimburses funeral-hosting relatives upon presentation of a hospital document or stamped BPA announcement alongside valid ID [3].

steps.title: Civil status records, tax status, and Ministry of Finance records
steps.html:
• Verify name spellings, dates of birth, and marital status across birth certificates, marriage certificates, national IDs, passports, and KPF membership cards well in advance, referencing vital registration rules under the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Ordinance [4][9].
  • Check taxpayer records, PAYE filings, or business clearances with Ministry of Finance and Economic Development (MFED) Tax Division (mfed.gov.ki) [13]. Confirm outstanding employer tax deductions or personal filings early, noting that Kiribati levies income tax and VAT on ongoing economic activity rather than a general inheritance or estate tax [13].
  • Store certified identity copies, bank passbooks, insurance contracts, and KPF account statements together in a secure file accessible to trusted family members [2][4][9].

steps.title: Cross-border legalisation and preparing a household dossier
steps.html:
• Confirm early whether foreign banks, insurers, or registries require official Kiribati documents: because Kiribati is not a Contracting Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, civil status certificates and court grants for overseas use require diplomatic or consular legalisation rather than a Hague Apostille [11]. Ask receiving foreign authorities what authentication and translation chain they accept before shipping originals abroad [11].
  • Compile a concise inventory listing local and overseas bank accounts, KPF membership number, employer HR contacts, tax identification details, and any Island Council or Lands Court files [4][8][13].
  • Verify local burial or repatriation constraints in advance if overseas family members expect international transport, because regional diplomatic reports note the absence of local embalming, cremation, or metal-casket facilities in Kiribati [10].
